children.text: Our Middle School program supports students through the important transition toward High School education. Middle School students experience a subject-based learning environment that encourages academic growth, independence, critical thinking, and personal responsibility.

The learning environment is designed to meet the developmental needs of middle school learners while providing a safe, supportive, and engaging atmosphere. Through a balanced academic program, dedicated teachers, and a strong sense of community, students are encouraged to build confidence, develop their skills, and prepare successfully for high school and beyond.

image.alt: SAIS - UAQ middle school students reading in the library

children.text: Transitions are carefully considered in the design of teaching and learning approaches. Teachers utilize a variety of instructional strategies tailored to students’ developmental stages and subject areas, fostering independence, critical thinking, creativity, and collaboration.

The curriculum is structured to provide a balanced blend of academic rigor, inquiry-based learning, and opportunities for exploration and self-discovery, ensuring that students thrive academically, socially, and emotionally throughout their educational journey.

heading.title:
Tailored Instruction for
Every Stage of Learning

image.alt: SAIS - UAQ middle school student playing keyboard during music class

children.text: The Middle School curriculums designed to deepen students’ subject knowledge while continuing to develop critical thinking, creativity, communication, and independent learning skills.
Students engage in a balanced academic program that includes core subjects, specialist instruction, electives, and enrichment opportunities that support both academic and personal growth.

image.alt: SAIS - UAQ students participating in class

children.text: In Middle School, assessment becomes more structured while continuing to focus on student development and continuous improvement. Students are assessed through quizzes, unit tests, formative assessments, projects, performance tasks, presentations, classwork, and project-based assessments.

Assessment practices are designed to measure students’ understanding, application of knowledge, analytical thinking, and ability to communicate their learning effectively. Teachers use assessment data to identify students’ strengths, address learning gaps, and provide targeted support when needed.

image.alt: SAIS - UAQ middle school students reviewing a book together

children.text: Middle School students also complete more formal assessments, including semester-based tests and final examinations where applicable. These assessments help prepare students for the academic expectations of High School.

In addition, students receive regular preparation for external assessments through skill-based practice, data-informed instruction, and exposure to international assessment-style questions that develop reasoning, problem-solving, and critical thinking skills.

children.text: At Sharjah American International School – UAQ Campus (SAIS - UAQ), the health and safety comprehensive on-site medical service staffed by:
A licensed doctor
Three qualified registered nurses
Three fully equipped clinics strategically located across campus

image.alt: SAIS - UAQ kindergarten students playing on ride-on toys

children.text: Whether class is in session or during extracurricular activities, our medical team provides:
Routine health screenings, vaccinations, and check-ups
Immediate first-aid and treatment for sports-related injuries
Management of acute illnesses and chronic conditions
Coordination of specialist referrals and follow-up care

Each clinic also serves as a hub for preventive health education; offering age-appropriate workshops and one-on-one guidance on balanced nutrition, personal hygiene, stress management, and injury prevention.

By embedding these services directly within the school environment, SAIS - UAQ fosters close, trusting relationships between students and healthcare professionals. This hands-on, holistic approach not only promotes better health outcomes but also supports every student’s emotional well-being and academic success.

children.text: Student life forms the essential foundation for personal and academic development. During this formative period, young people encounter diverse situations that prepare them for future challenges. They develop crucial skills in respect and self-discipline while building relationships with peers and educators.

heading.title: A Foundation for Growth and Development

children.text: School life represents a joyful time when students can explore, form friendships, acquire skills, and embrace experiences without the weight of adult responsibilities.
Within the school environment, students learn the importance of punctuality, adherence to rules, and fulfillment of responsibilities while gaining knowledge and developing new capabilities.

image.alt: Student Government Association

children.text: The guidance received during student life transforms young people into well-rounded individuals. Teachers and parents provide direction, helping students distinguish between beneficial and detrimental choices.
This golden period of development is when children’s minds, comparable to clay are most receptive to positive molding and influence.

image.alt: SAIS - UAQ student presenting to the Student Congress

children.text: The school environment facilitates holistic learning beyond academics. Students develop proper manners, positive behaviors, discipline, and punctuality. With appropriate education and guidance, they mature into responsible adults prepared for real-world challenges.

children.text: Student life establishes the groundwork for both character development and knowledge acquisition. It teaches children about consistency, obedience, sincerity, and perseverance.
Through social interactions, students enhance their interpersonal skills while learning to respect diversity while maintaining their own values and principles.

children.text: At Sharjah American International School – UAQ Campus (SAIS - UAQ), we are committed to nurturing the holistic well-being of both students and staff.

Our comprehensive Well-Being Framework rests on four pillars (emotional, social, mental, and physical health) and is woven into every aspect of school life, from classroom routines to campus-wide initiatives. Through these layered supports and proactive initiatives, SAIS - UAQ fosters an environment where every member of our community (students and staff alike) feels seen, supported, and empowered to thrive.

image.alt: SAIS - UAQ students smiling in class

children.text: Licensed Counseling Team:
We employ a full-time school counselor and assistant counselors who provide individual check-ins, small-group workshops, and crisis intervention as needed.
Open-Door Policy:
Every student and staff member may schedule drop-in sessions or refer peers, ensuring timely support for academic stress, interpersonal conflicts, or personal challenges.
Parent & Family Outreach:
Counselors host regular webinars and one-on-one conferences to equip families with strategies for supporting well-being at home.

image.alt: SAIS - UAQ student smiling while working on a craft activity

children.text: Curriculum Integration: Our SEL curriculum runs from Kindergarten through Grade 12, with age-appropriate competencies, self-awareness, self-management, social awareness, relationship skills, and responsible decision-making taught through homeroom lessons, art, and PE sessions.
SEL Coaches: Trained staff lead fortnightly classroom circles, role-play activities, and reflective journaling to help students practice empathy, resilience, and effective communication.

image.alt: SAIS - UAQ teacher guiding two students through a hands-on SEL activity

children.text: Mindfulness & Restorative Practices:
Daily “mindful minutes” and monthly restorative circles give students and teachers tools to regulate emotions and resolve conflicts constructively.
Professional Development:
Faculty participate in ongoing workshops on SEL facilitation techniques, stress-management strategies, and inclusive classroom practices.
Peer-Support Networks:
Student wellbeing ambassadors collaborate with counselors to organize “buddy check-ins” and peer-led wellness clubs.

image.alt: SAIS - UAQ students exploring classroom learning activities

children.text: Healthy Lifestyle Week:
A dedicated week each term featuring myriad activities.
Annual Sports Day & Fitness Clubs:
From track relays to yoga and dance clubs, we promote daily physical activity as a cornerstone of mental and physical health.
Mental Health Awareness Days:
Quarterly events with guest speakers, stress-relief stations (e.g., art-therapy corners, relaxation tents), and student-led panels.

image.alt: SAIS - UAQ students playing volleyball on the school court

children.text: Speaking Corner:
Each section features a dedicated Speaking Corner (part of our SEL program) where students can share thoughts, practice communication skills, and seek peer or counselor support.
Collaborative Planning:
Teachers and counselors co-design lesson plans that infuse academic topics with social-emotional check-points and opportunities for cooperative learning.
Feedback Loops:
Regular surveys of students and staff inform ongoing refinements to our Well-Being Framework, ensuring it remains responsive to community needs.
